findings.reason: the deliverable must be bounded to untracked directories outside every declared root, or §78 hands the worker a measure that a guard-crippling change passes.
findings.text: §78's deliverable is written for every untracked directory, but `_repository_tree_boundary_violations` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:754-895) builds a violation only from a changed entry whose path lies under the run's declared roots, and it finds that entry by comparing per-file snapshot entries (`_snapshot_entries(after) - _snapshot_entries(before)`); a stray file a run declares at, say, `dir/file.py` inside an untracked 20,000-file directory can therefore be seen only by enumerating that directory, so "costs the same however many files lie under the checkout's untracked directories" and "still refuses what it refuses today" cannot both hold in the deliverable's stated generality — a worker can satisfy the wall-time arm by dropping the file-level walk — `--untracked-files=normal` reports an untracked directory as one entry — and the "every refusal still fires" arm will still pass, because every stray a test asserts today is an untracked file at a tree root, reported by name in normal mode as well (`tests/test_crew_promotion_scope.py:216` writes `late_tree / "stray.txt"`; `tests/test_crew_boundary_waiver.py:105,140,166` and `tests/test_crew_promotion_scope.py:139,177` write `allowed.txt`), so no existing refusal would catch a stray filed at a declared file path inside an untracked directory

findings.reason: the author must decide which clause yields — either the reading keeps every field and the cost clause is replaced by a bound on classification work, or the fields shrink and the deliverable says so — otherwise the node is dispatched against a measure that no implementation can meet.
findings.text: §79's done-when requires both that the count of files opened under other runs' directories at 100 pointers is no more than the count at 10 plus 10 and that the fleet fields recorded on the promoted row equal the base revision's, while `_fleet_state_reading` (reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:1022-1067) records `unreconciled_runs`, `actionable_runs` and `actionable_classifications`, each derived by running `recovery.classify_pointer` and `_drain_row` over every live pointer, and the reading is deliberately kept out of the ledger so no cached fleet index exists to serve those fields; producing the base's fields therefore requires visiting each of the 90 added pointers, which is the growth the count arm forbids, so the two arms of the measure cannot both pass and the node has no reachable endpoint

response_events.note: §78 is bounded to untracked directories outside every declared root, and adds a case where a stray at a declared path inside an untracked directory is still refused.
